Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
34-year-old man with 4-day history of severe headache, subjective fever, generalized myalgia, and diffuse blanching pruritic rash after recent travel to Thailand.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Severe headache for 4 days; subjective fever/chills (temperature not measured).  
• Associated symptoms: Generalized muscle aches, feeling cold, diffuse red itchy blanching rash.  
• Pertinent negatives: No photophobia, no neck stiffness/pain on movement, no vomiting, no cough/cold symptoms, no ear pain, no focal weakness or sensory changes.  
• Past medical history: Denies chronic medical or surgical conditions.  
• Medications: Paracetamol and Ibuprofen ‑ dose/route/frequency not documented; no regular medications.  
• Allergies: Denies drug allergies.  
• Social/travel: Returned from Thailand ~1 week ago; multiple mosquito bites; friend also unwell. No other social history provided.

Examination:
Vitals: Not assessed (teleconsultation).  
Physical exam: Not performed.

Impression:
Febrile viral illness post-travel (differentials include dengue fever and other mosquito-borne infections); meningitis less likely but not excluded.

Plan:
• Urgent in-person assessment at GP hub within the next few hours for full physical exam and vitals.  
• Possible referral to hospital for further evaluation and blood tests if indicated after examination.  
• Continue symptomatic relief with Paracetamol/Ibuprofen as needed.  
• Advise patient to seek emergency care immediately if symptoms worsen (persistent fever, non-blanching rash, photophobia, neck stiffness, vomiting, weakness).  
• No additional prescriptions given during teleconsultation.

Quality checks:
● Missing but expected: Objective temperature, full vitals, medication doses, vaccination/travel prophylaxis history, family history, alcohol/smoking history.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; minimal background noise, no significant inaudible sections.
